analysis: Integration pass over 13 units. Docs (changelog.d/coordinator-traffic-verdict.md, docs/provider/cli-reference.md Traffic bullet ~1045-1062, docs/provider/troubleshooting.md lines 83 and 143) and tests are non-executable. Production changes are diagnostics/recovery only: ServingReadiness gains .unconfirmed, refusalMaxAge (60s), statusGraceSeconds (90s) and a routed-request override; ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head 429-430) calls noteCoordinatorRequest() on .inferenceRequest, which stamps DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt (an optional timestamp, schema unchanged); superviseServingAuthorization delegates to ServingReadiness.verdict; DoctorRunner/StatusCommand render .unconfirmed as info; handleTrustStatus gains a receivedAt parameter. None of this touches request admission, decryption, grants or attestation. Coordinator-owned authorization (TB-011, A-016, T-052/T-053) is unchanged. Per unit summaries, tests assert that explicit untrusted status and an expired App Attest lease still block despite a routed request. The new fields add no secrets; the activity timestamp is minor local metadata. Residual unverified items, since the ServingReadiness body, noteCoordinatorRequest and the caller of handleTrustStatus were not fully supplied: (1) a routed request can only suppress local recovery re-registration, not grant serving, so the impact is bounded to availability (T-057); (2) .inferenceRequest arrives only from the trusted coordinator channel, so the spoofing risk looks low; (3) logSinkForTesting should not be reachable in release paths; (4) all switch callers should handle .unconfirmed non-permissively. None is established as a regression, so no findings. Recommend a later look at ServingReadiness.swift and the receivedAt callers.
